releases.title: Bootstrap Paradox
releases.label: Comet Collective
releases.blurb:
Slix make their debut on Comet Collective with Bootstrap Paradox, a three-track EP built around a simple idea: a signal sent from the future to the present.
The contact begins with a synthesizer sent back through time, a message from our future selves. As the signal is brought into the present and the tracks begin to take shape, the sound starts to distort, break apart and evolve, giving birth to the second chapter, Hyper Distortion.
The final track, Prometheus, marks what comes after the contact. The beginning of a new era as the portal opens and the signal reaches its destination.

Bootstrap Paradox is the story of a message travelling through time and what happens when we answer it.

releases.title: Blue Lion
releases.label: Comet Collective
releases.blurb:
Blue Lion marks the first collaboration between Israeli artists Azul and LIBAAX.

The EP features two original tracks that showcase different sides of their shared sound.

The title track, Blue Lion, is a high-energy, dancefloor-focused production built around driving grooves, deep atmospheres, and a patient progression that leads into an intense peak of raw energy.

The second track, Mixed Call, offers a brighter and more uplifting contrast. Inspired by a memorable moment the two artists shared at a festival, the track captures that feeling through a lighter, more melodic approach while maintaining the energy of the collaboration.

Blue Lion marks the beginning of a new creative partnership between Azul and LIBAAX, with more music from the duo on the way.

releases.label: Comet Collective
releases.blurb:
Comet Collective Compilation returns with a second chapter shaped by individual voices and a shared sense of direction. Each track stands on its own, yet together they form a subtle dialogue, a space where emerging energy and familiar presence meet naturally, without hierarchy.

Drawn from both within and around the collective, the selection reflects a wider circle of connection, carefully brought together by Jahrin through a perspective rooted in the foundation of the collective itself. A collection built on intuition, trust, and the idea of giving sound the room to evolve on its own terms.

On one side – a beat bouncing like a kid with too much energy and not enough rules.
On the other side – an old man roaming in a black coat, punctual, mostly silent, but moving perfectly.
Both are groovy. Neither apologizes. And both – are me.
